descriptions.title: FastAPI dashboard — server-rendered, no SPA
descriptions.body: The Hive Dashboard (engine/hive/dashboard/server.py, ~7800 lines) renders each page as a Python function returning an HTML string — no React, no client-side router, no JS build step. This is intentional: the dashboard is an internal development/operations tool, not a customer product. Server-rendered pages are trivial to debug (view-source shows real state), and AdminLTE v4 over CDN supplies the visual polish. The same app serves the JSON REST API (/api/tasks, /api/health, /api/usage/*, /api/library/*) that the few interactive pages (kanban, Documentation Brain) call.

descriptions.title: QI Brain — SQLite + ChromaDB knowledge substrate
descriptions.body: The Brain (engine/brain/api.py, :9011) keeps two stores in lockstep. SQLite (data/qi_brain.db, 24 tables) is the authoritative catalog of 491 decisions, 394 features, 564 sessions, 239 project-state snapshots, 921 docs, and 2203 doc relationships. ChromaDB (engine/brain/qi_memory/) holds the vector index for semantic search across four collections. Writes go to SQL first (durable) and embed best-effort — if Chroma or Ollama is down the row is still cataloged and re-embedded later. Because Chroma's PersistentClient isn't consistent across processes, POST /api/admin/reload_memory drops the cached store so out-of-process harvests are served fresh without a restart.

descriptions.title: NSSM service fabric + the elevation broker
descriptions.body: Every long-running QI piece is a Windows service prefixed QI_ and managed by a single standardized NSSM at engine/bin/nssm.exe. QI Hive owns QI_Dashboard, QI_BrainAPI, QI_Elevate, QI_HiveIngest, QI_HiveApply, QI_HiveInspectorDrain, and QI_DashboardTunnel. The hard problem is autonomy: Claude sessions run as a normal user but restarting a service needs admin, and UAC blocks unattended loops. The QI_Elevate broker runs as LocalSystem, watches commands/pending/*.json, and executes only regex-whitelisted commands (no shell, no expansion) — so qi_service.py can restart any service from any session with zero prompts. qi_service.py prefers sc.exe over nssm for start/stop after an OpenService access-denied discovery.

descriptions.title: Cloudflare named tunnels — permanent public URLs
descriptions.body: Before 2026-06-20 every public app used a quick tunnel whose *.trycloudflare.com URL changed on each restart — breaking the dashboard's link tiles and any saved webhook. The migration (engine/tunnels/migrate_named_tunnels.py, tunnels.json) moved every app to a static named tunnel on the new domain quiddityinnovations.com, one tunnel per product for fault isolation. The Hive itself lives at hive.quiddityinnovations.com. link_collector.py and static_urls.url_for_port() resolve each service's permanent URL from tunnels.json, with quick-tunnel log-tailing kept only as a fallback.

descriptions.title: The sub-agent system + Dispatch Protocol
descriptions.body: QI Hive turns Claude Code into an eight-role team: architect (Opus, design only), builder (Sonnet, implementation), inspector (Sonnet, read-only review), ops/scout/scribe/tester (Haiku), and the librarian over the doc index. The agents are Claude Code sub-agents (.claude/agents/hive-*.md) invoked via Agent(subagent_type=hive-<role>). The main thread is the dispatcher — DISPATCH_PROTOCOL.md maps each task type to a role and codifies the design->build->inspect->scribe workflow and the anti-patterns (no architect reasoning in the main thread, never skip the inspector, honest agent attribution, one level of delegation deep). Model tiering keeps Opus tokens for reasoning and Haiku for triage.

descriptions.title: The registry + the Six Laws (governance)
descriptions.body: qi_registry.json is the constitution's first law — the single source of truth for every project's port block, path, status, and integration contract (25 entries today). qi_validator.py checks a project against it; qi_new_project.py registers-then-scaffolds so no project is ever hand-built non-compliant. The Six Laws (QI_Architecture_Principles.md) bind all projects: registry truth, the /health+/version+/info module contract, independence with graceful degradation, contract-first APIs, an always-current registry, and Law 6 — owner override plus mandatory best-practice surfacing. The Inspector (engine/hive/inspector/inspector.py) enforces these continuously, auto-fixing safe drift and filing dispatches for the rest.

descriptions.title: Documentation Brain — federated index + knowledge graph
descriptions.body: doc_harvester.py walks every documentation source across the ecosystem and catalogs each file into the docs table (921 rows) without moving it — storage stays federated. It derives typed edges into doc_relationships (2203) to build a TheBrain-style Plex graph linking docs, projects, decisions, features, and sessions, and embeds the text into the qi_docs Chroma collection for semantic search. The harvest is idempotent (content-hash skips), marks logs/minutes/version-history stale after 45 days, and excludes archive snapshots so duplicate-group noise never crowds live docs. The hive-librarian agent and the /library dashboard page are the retrieval front ends.

descriptions.title: LLM usage tracking — no API keys required
descriptions.body: Claude Code writes a JSONL log for every conversation under ~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl, one JSON object per turn with token counts and model. usage_stats.py reads these files directly — no Anthropic API call, no auth — applies the public token pricing table (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku input/output plus cache-token multipliers), and produces per-day, per-project, and per-model cost breakdowns. It also computes the savings from routing work to local Ollama models instead of Claude. Results are cached briefly so dashboard page loads stay fast.
